History & Physical (Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
50-year-old overweight male with type 2 diabetes and hypertension presents via telephone with 4–5 days of viral-type upper respiratory symptoms (dry–then–mildly productive cough, rhinorrhoea, sore throat, myalgias, subjective fevers, and new shortness of breath); safety-net delay prescription for amoxicillin issued.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “Not feeling well” – cough, cold, run-down.  
• Onset/Timeline: Began Saturday evening (~5 days ago) while out for dinner; gradual progression.  
• Symptom details  
  – Cough: Mainly dry; slightly worse in mornings; occasional “mucky phlegm.”  
  – Upper airway: Runny nose/sniffles; sore throat (also shouts at football); mild ear dullness.  
  – Respiratory: Shortness of breath described as “not good,” no chest pain.  
  – Constitutional: Subjective fever, night sweats, chills (blanket on/off).  
  – GI: One day of diarrhoea at onset, now resolved; no nausea or vomiting; appetite preserved.  
  – Musculoskeletal: Generalised joint/muscle stiffness when bending.  
• Exacerbating factors: None identified; throat possibly aggravated by shouting.  
• Relieving measures: Increased fluids; no thermometer or medications used yet.  
• Review of systems – Pertinent negatives (as asked): No chest pain, no vomiting, no persistent GI issues.  

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus – on metformin; no complications discussed.  
• Hypertension – on lisinopril; prior elevated BP noted.  
• Overweight/obesity (self-reported “spare tyre”).  
• No known drug allergies (NKDA).  

Medications:
• Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Aspirin intermittently – dose/route/frequency not documented.  

Social History:
• Lives with wife; adult children have left home.  
• Employment: Factory worker manufacturing steel parts.  
• Alcohol: ~9 pints beer/week (4 on Saturday, remainder Sunday).  
• Tobacco: Occasional smoker; currently switching to vaping, actively cutting down.  
• No illicit drug use mentioned.  

Family History:
• Not discussed.  

Physical Examination:
(telephone consultation – no vitals or in-person exam performed)  

Investigations:
• None obtained; no labs or imaging ordered.  

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Acute viral upper respiratory infection / influenza-like illness (possible early bacterial lower respiratory tract infection)  
  • Evidence: 5-day history of cough, rhinorrhoea, sore throat, myalgias, subjective fever; mild sputum and dyspnoea raise concern for progression.  
  • Plan:  
    – Conservative care: Rest, maintain hydration, regular paracetamol for fever/aches.  
    – Delayed antibiotic prescription: Amoxicillin – “one tablet three times daily” to start if symptoms not improving in 24–48 h or worsening (dose strength not documented).  
    – Safety-net advice: If increasing breathlessness, persistent fever, or no improvement by next week, re-contact GP for review.  
    – Advise COVID-19/flu testing per local guidance if available (aligned with viral differential).  

Issue 2 – Type 2 diabetes mellitus  
  • Continue metformin; monitor blood glucose more frequently during illness; seek care for hyperglycaemia or hypoglycaemia.  

Issue 3 – Hypertension / cardiovascular risk & lifestyle  
  • Continue lisinopril.  
  • Encourage smoking cessation (continue vaping reduction strategy).  
  • Discuss alcohol moderation and weight management at future review.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Acute viral upper respiratory infection / Influenza-like illness (incl. COVID-19) – High likelihood: classic constellation of acute cough, rhinorrhoea, myalgias, subjective fever over 5 days.  
2. Community-acquired pneumonia – Moderate likelihood: productive sputum, dyspnoea, fevers, diabetic risk; lack of objective findings or exam limits confirmation.  
3. Acute bronchitis – Moderate likelihood: sub-acute cough following URI; overlaps with viral picture; usually self-limiting.  
(Other lower-probability considerations in DDx – ACE-inhibitor cough, CHF – currently less consistent.)

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: No objective vitals, lung exam, or pulse oximetry; no documented temperature; no allergy verification beyond “none known”; no current glucose/BP readings; family history absent.  
● Transcript vs DDx conflicts: None significant noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear but conversational; no background noise; lacked physical exam due to telehealth format.
